attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Patel, MD
Department: Psychiatry
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Cessation of menstrual periods for four months in the setting of increased athletic training

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
She reports that her menarche occurred at age 13 and her cycles were regular until about four months ago. She is a competitive cross-country runner for her university and recently began training twice a day in preparation for nationals. She reports eating "very clean" and avoids processed foods, dairy, and most fats. She admits to counting calories and usually eats only one large salad and a protein shake per day. Her friends have commented on how thin she's gotten, but she believes this is necessary to stay competitive. She denies depression but does report occasional lightheadedness during workouts and always feeling cold. She has not been sexually active and denies any history of abnormal vaginal bleeding or discharge.

MEDICATIONS:
She does not use any medications or supplements.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Generalized anxiety disorder
- Maternal grandmother: Postmenopausal osteoporosis
- Father: Essential hypertension

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Rare (1-2 drinks per year). Occupation: University student, NCAA Division I cross-country runner.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical exam, her BMI is 16.1. She appears thin, with dry skin, brittle hair, and lanugo on her upper arms. Breast development is Tanner stage IV. Pelvic exam is unremarkable, with normal external genitalia.

LABORATORY DATA:
Pregnancy test is negative. Lab evaluation reveals low serum estradiol, FSH, and LH levels. TSH and prolactin are within normal limits.

IMAGING:
A DEXA scan shows low bone mineral density at the lumbar spine.
